nom: The Ordinary Glucoside Gentle Foaming Cleanser for Oily Skin

segments.oily: Reviewers with oily, combination-oily, or acne-prone oily skin generally report the cleanser works well, cleans thoroughly without over-drying, and helps control breakouts, though some note it is harder to foam once the T-zone is oily and may require double cleansing.
segments.dry: Reviewers who identify as dry or mature-dry report the most negative experiences, describing dryness, tightness, eyelid dryness and splitting, and needing heavy moisturizer afterward, though a few dry-skin reviewers say it did not strip them.
segments.combination: Combination-skin reviewers report mixed results, with some finding it balances well across zones and others finding it dries out the drier areas, especially in fall/winter.
segments.sensitive: Sensitive-skin reviewers, including those with rosacea or eczema, frequently report the cleanser is unusually gentle and non-irritating, calming for reactive or hormonal-acne-prone sensitive skin, though a couple report residue or dryness.
segments.normal: Normal-skin reviewers describe it as a solid, no-frills cleanser that works best used sparingly, without complaints of irritation.
segments.mature: Mature-skin reviewers are split: one describes severe eyelid dryness and splitting leading her to stop use, while another in her 40s reports it helped clear blemishes and was dermatologist-recommended.

concerns.aging: A mature reviewer in her 40s reports the cleanser, on dermatologist recommendation, helped with blemishes appearing at that age; another mature reviewer reports severe dryness and eyelid splitting and stopped use.
concerns.dehydration: Many reviewers, mostly with dry or combination-dry skin, report increased dryness, tightness, or the need for heavier moisturizer afterward; several others with oily or normal skin report no dehydration and even find it leaves skin feeling moisturized.
concerns.redness: One reviewer with rosacea and an oily T-zone reports the cleanser feels calming rather than irritating, unlike products marketed for oily or sensitive skin.
concerns.barrier: A reviewer who believed she had dry, barrier-compromised, cystic-prone skin reports her skin turned out to be more normal-to-oily and no longer feels tight after using this cleanser; another with eyelid eczema reports it calmed her flare-up.
concerns.spots: Several reviewers with hormonal or cystic acne report clearer skin, reduced new blemishes, and improved scarring over weeks to months of use; no reviewer reports the cleanser itself causing spots, though one reviewer switched away citing breakouts from a different (squalane) product for context.
concerns.blemishes: Numerous acne-prone reviewers, including teens and adults with hormonal or cystic acne, report breakouts subsiding and skin clearing, often combined with salicylic acid or niacinamide serums; one reviewer reports the cleanser made her skin break out and dried it excessively.
concerns.oiliness: Oily-skin reviewers, including one in her late 30s with very oily skin, report it cleans thoroughly without leaving skin greasy or as dried out as other cleansers they compare it to (e.g., Neutrogena, Cerave).

extraits.texte: I brought this in November. I have dry mature skin. After a few days of using I noticed my eyelids got very dry and itchy. Then they started to split. I had no idea what was going on, so I carried on using it. After a few more weeks of very sore eyes I thought maybe it's this foam wash so I stopped using it and my eyes cleared up. So I tried using it again just recently and and again my eye lids dried up and started splitting. So I won't be recommending this product to anyone. I do however like your other products that I use and will have to look to see if you have another facewash that might be more suitable for my dry skin.

my highly reactive, still oily at 48 yrs old but gets dry in the winter with retinols face needed sowmthing more gentle for the upcoming cold. i usually an i juice beauty brightening cleanser user. i have started using this cleanser at night and my face really appreciates it. neatly everything breaks me out to some degree, this has not. not drying but not overly loaded with skin conditioners. my skin just feels normal, not tight. i will keep using now.

My skin is very sensitive, I have rosacea, and my t-zone is extremely oily. Fun! Products made for oily skin are too harsh; products made for sensitive skin are too emollient. This makes my skin feel clean and calm. (Probably not great for dry skin.)

I'm in my late 30s with superrr oily skin and Hispanic. This super cleans my face and does not leave it dryed out like Neutrogena did. Will definitely keep buying this for life. Also it's super consentrated so you only need about half a grape size.

I have eczema on my face and often struggle with finding a gentle cleanser that works with my dry skin and am often terrified of trying new skin products. I swore by the Tula milk cleanser until it was sadly discontinued and decided to try The Ordinary glucoside cleanser since their moisturizing products work well with my skin. I'm so happy I decided to give it a try! No dryness, flakyness or burning and for more than half the price of Tula! Definitely my new go-to :) If you struggle with eczema or sensitive skin definitely give it a try!

extraits.titre: Cleanser go to for combo to oily skin
extraits.texte: This cleanser has been go to the last year and I've seen my skin transform from frequent use. It's affordable and my skin has loved it. It does what it says and smooths out the skin, my skin isn't perfect but it's healthy and clear the only concern that I have that this cleanser can't fix is my closed commodones. Note to anyone reading this: I only cleanse at night with this and I also double cleanse daily with a double cleanser. For my skin type I find double cleansing works best at reducing my acne and is what you need to do remove the sunscreen you've had on all day. Use this cleanser second after the oil cleanser! I'm not saying this cleanser shouldn't be used AM aswell it's just what works for my skin. You know your skin better than anybody. Give it a try if you are looking for a foaming cleanser it's not over stripping and really can clear a breakout with the good follow up routine in a matter of days.

extraits.titre: Off-putting smell and doesn't really do anything for my skin
extraits.texte: I'd say I have dry skin, but my nose will get oily - so I guess combination, but not in the T-zone, just my nose. I've also read that this isn't great for dry skin, but I've had other foaming cleansers and they work so well with my skin, so I thought I'd give this a try. Right away, it smells like wet dog. I know it's fragrance free, but this is just hard to use on my face with a scent like that.. And after using it for a while, it really did nothing for my skin. It didn't feel clean, my skin didn't feel smooth or soft, but also not dried out. Just felt like my skin if I woke up and didn't wash it. Oh, it also really didn't foam unless I REALLY rubbed my hands together which is not what I'm used to from a FOAMING cleanser lol. I dunno, it just didn't work for me so I wouldn't be buying again. Shame because it's my first product from the Ordinary and now I'm not sure if I'll try others because I don't think they fit my skin type.
